newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: OPINION - Strategy for Philippine stocks - Pryce Securities.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Strategy for Philippine stocks - Pryce Securities.

text.p: By Jonas Ferrer, vice-president, research, Pryce Securities
Suggested strategy under enervating market conditions:

This is an assessment of the domestic bourse's prospects amid the current regional shakedown that has sapped the erstwhile overwhelming investor enthusiasm which enabled the Phisix (Philippine Stock Exchange index) to momentarily attain its all-time peak of 3,374.40 last July 5. That rise was dramatic, starting from 2,578.97 on January 2.

In order to devise a suitable strategy which can withstand the prevailing scepticism, I have engaged several resource people from the academe, government and corporate fronts (including fellow brokers) in lively discourses delving into the solid fundamental underpinnings which major players seem to have been ignoring for the past few months.
Taking their observations as appropriate inputs, I have come up with several conclusions with which I hope to guide perplexed investors in re-configuring their battered portfolios.

1) The dumping of real estate counters has largely been overdone as part of the massive liquidation in the region. Notwithstanding the still favourable demand supply situation (including those of the high-end residential and office condominiums), foreign fund managers have indiscriminately unloaded majority of their holdings in the real estate sector due to fears that the industry may be overheating when ranged against the Thai and Malaysian experience during the past few years.

However, distinct domestic factors such as the rapid reorganization of property developments (which has spawned notable price appreciation in most provincial areas), the liberalisation of major industries like banking, insurance, mining, oil refining, information technology and probably retail (which should redound to incremental demand to reinforce the industry's organic growth), and the reverse capital flight along with the continued hike in remittances from overseas workers should continually prop up the sector.

Although it may be unwise (more of suicidal) to go against the selling tide, I sincerely believe that upon the conclusion of the current shakeout, opportunistic trading windows in battered but fundamentally sturdy counters are the order of the day.

I reckon that after a significant depreciation in prices, a modest to sizable retracement is in the offing which should benefit those who position in premier counters such as Ayala Land B, Filinvest Land, C&P Homes, and Fil-Estate Land along with oversold secondaries Universal Rightfield (speculative), Belle Corp, Megaworld, Empire East Land (trading), Robinsons Land B and Mongradon International, Guoco Holdings and Centenntial City, SM Development Corp (trading), Waterfront Philippines (specutive) and Mondragon (on weakness).

However to avoid the pitfalls that such short-run rallies may bring forth, it would be prudent to unload the less fundamentally sound issues after a substantial technical rally and retain only the key scrips which possess enticing earnings prospects, solid management, considerable landbanks, and excellent investor rapport.

2) Since other segments were similarly drowned by the selling wave, participants may also discover attractive buying opportunities after major successive dips from hereon. In this regard, I present my reading of the outlook of the other key sectors which are worth considering at this point.

Construction/Infrastructure-related: Robust demand situation derived primarily from the sustained boom in the property sector should provide issues such as House of Investments, DMCI, Bacnotan Consolidated, Benpres Holdings, First Philippine Holdings (long-term), EEI Corp South East Asia Cement (trading), and Alsons Consolidated (on weakness), sizeable upsides before year-end.

Food/Consumer-related: Despite puny earnings growth rates (when ranged against the other industries), the fourth quarter surge in consumer spending may provide the much needed support to induce the widely anticipated run-up in food entities San Miguel Corp A (due to the planned shift of the Coconut Industry Fund's existing "B" holding, Universal Robina (on weakness) JG Summit (for a more diversified participation), and La Tondena (long-term).
Meanwhile, consumer-oriented scrips Uniwide, Solid Group, and SM Prime Holdings have slumped to levels which I deem fail to appreciate their immense earnings potential and purported asset repricing.
Banking: Favorable interest rate regime (which should intensify demand for loans and more sophisticated products to support the expansion programs of major firms).

Keener competition, expanded business scope and coverage and a proposed 2 percent cut in the reserve requirement as early as the first quarter of next year, are seen as the main factors which should dictate the reorganization, reorientation, and reconfiguration of the capacities and strategies of industry players.

Given this backdrop, I am encouraged by the promising potentials of Philippine National Bank (ongoing reorganization which involves the disposition of foreclosed assets amounting to about 3.0 billion pesos and redundancy program aimed at reducing manpower by at least 15 percent should result into a more competitive, leaner, and efficient institution capable of competing head-on with its peer bank as early as mid-1997).

Bank of the Philippine Islands merger with City Trust should elevate the bank back into the limelight in terms of asset size, market capitalization, and equity base along with the creation of a retail market dynamo, and PCIBank (sharp, enterprising, and innovative management gives the institution the competitive advantage in succesfully carving a more fulfilling earnings scenario.

As for the other notable issues, I advise investors to pare holdings of Meropolitan Bank (concerns of probable leadership crisis post George Ty and great dependence on second-tier client base which is highly susceptible to competition may weigh down earnings, deposit, and loan growth overshadowing intensified efforts to expand business scope and coverage), and position in Security Bank, and Asia Trust after price downturns.
Others: Any bourse participant who is steadfast in his belief of the sustainability of the Philippine growth story may be willing accumulators of blue chips Meralco and Petron (trading).

In addition, inspite of lingering concerns on the negative demographics that is gripping the shipping industry, we are still ardent buyers of shipping giant William Gothong long-term) and domestic information technology stalwarts (in order of preference) Saztec Philippines, Music Semiconductors, and Ionics Circuits (trading).
As for the previously outpermforming tertiaries, assuming that there is a prolonged consolidation after an expected retracement, I am not too keen on repositioning on such speculative counters.
CONCLUSION

Even if I am admittedly somewhat shaken by the prevailing porfolio realignment, I would like to underscore my undaunted confidence in our market especially in the medium to longer-haul. Akin to past downturns which have incessantly dampened sentiments over the past two years (the latest of which came last November when the market slipped to its all-time low near 2,100 as a consequence of a spiral in the inflation rate), we percieve the current situation as part of the financial hiccups that occasionally rattle emerging markets (especially those in the nascent stage of economic recovery like ours) when major institutional investors (foremost of which are international-based mutual funds) undertake a massive shifting of funds to more mature markets such as the United States and Europe.

As part of a global trend, with small investors continually infusing thier savings into mutual funds which are geared to search for earnings sources which are genarally above market rates coinciding with an eventual slowdown in the advance of major bourses, the current downturn in the Asia Pacific region (the Philippines included) provides more opportunities to pile up on attractively priced issues with unstinting and robust underlying fundamentals.

Based on our experience and simulations, there are only (under normal circumstances) three or four clear-cut occasions in a given year when patient and undeterred players are successful in generating hefty gains.
These gratifying moments usually occur when there are aberrations in the overall scheme of things that cloud the underlying strength of the system.
In our present case, the overwhelming departure of porfolio investments is the major event that has clouded our dramatic inroads in improving our fundamental status.

Among the essential factors which investors should be on the look out for in determining the future direction of the market are: Sustained Growth in Third Quarter Corporate results (which should dispel whatever apprehensions of a purported earnings slowdown), Encouraging Economic Indicators (primarily the inflation rate, GNP growth rate, reserve and base money aggregates, GIR, and BOP and budget positions), the Proposed Reduction in the Reserve Requirement (by as much as 2%) from the current 17%, the much awaited passage of the compreshensive tax reform program (with special attention on the shift back to a purely specific tax system in lieu of the present advalorem tax scheme), The Full deregulation of the Oil Industry, and the liberalization of the Retail Trade Industry.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent those of the author only. They should not be seen to represent the view of Reuters)
